jobs.title: Energy Analyst Intern (Economics) - Summer 2027 at The Brattle Group
jobs.description: Employer: The Brattle Group Expires: 10/20/2026 Please note that while we accept applications for our internship position starting in the fall, we will not begin actively contacting candidates for interviews until/after November 2026.Our Summer Internship Opportunity:This internship program will provide you with the opportunity to apply the economic concepts you’re learning in the classroom in a professional services setting. It will also help you to improve your research and data analysis skills as well as learn to manage and prioritize tasks. You will work side by side with internationally recognized experts in financial economics, corporate finance, energy, competition, and regulatory economics.Energy Analyst Intern RoleAs an Energy Analyst intern at The Brattle Group, you will be integral to our project teams, collaborating with senior consultants and experts. Your responsibilities will include:Quantitative Models and Solutions: You'll build models and create innovative data-based solutions for clients using programming languages, such as Excel, R, Python, GAMS, Stata, and VBA (e.g. conducting data and statistical analysis, econometric analysis, building interactive dashboards, etc.).Qualitative Research and Literature Review: You'll conduct comprehensive energy analysis, including market analysis, literature reviews, document examination, and writing memos to provide insights and support expert reports.Preparing Client Deliverables: You’ll contribute to client deliverables, including presentations and memos, with figures, quantitative results, and novel findings.Supporting Expert Witnesses: You'll assist in preparing expert reports and presentations, helping our experts present complex economic and financial concepts clearly in legal and regulatory contexts.Collaborating with Team Members: Effective communication and teamwork are critical. You'll work closely with colleagues at all levels, contributing to the development of robust and innovative solutions for our clients.Typical Assignments Might Include:Analyzing electricity, natural gas, and other energy markets and applying this information in financial, legal, and policy settings.Building novel financial, economic, statistical, and operational models using a variety of tools.Coauthoring publications and being a part of presentation teams.Communicating research and analyses to project team members and clients.Developing, maintaining, and running power system models, including capacity expansion and security-constrained production cost models.Providing in-depth regulatory and policy research and summarizing insights through literature review.Thinking critically about analysis results and discussing findings with an internal team.You will work in a collaborative atmosphere where dedication to project success and individual career and professional development are emphasized. You will have the opportunity to discover where your strengths and interests lie and how you can best apply your skills. The work environment is collegial; and there is significant, on-going contact between senior and junior staff.The CandidateThe ideal candidates will be pursuing, and possess:An undergraduate degree in a quantitative discipline (e.g. economics, computer science, data science, and mathematics), with strong academic performance. Successful applicants typically have a GPA of 3.7 or higher (based on a 4.0 scale).Great teamwork and leadership skills. Our project work is done almost exclusively on teams, so it’s critical that our EA interns work well with others.Intellectual curiosity and creativity. We are looking for candidates who consistently want to learn more and approach problems with creativity.A high degree of ownership and commitment. Successful EA interns are committed to delivering their best work product, taking ownership of their work, and engaging in excellent client services.Strong communication skills.Additionally, we look for candidates who:Have completed or will complete a course with a climate or energy focus.To Be Considered for the Energy Analyst Intern Position:Please submit the following materials as soon as possible via the application below.Cover LetterResumeTranscript(s) (unofficial copies accepted)To streamline the process, please use your school-issued email address on your application.The anticipated base gross salary for this position in Boston, MA is $1,850.00 per week.EQUAL OPPORTUNITYThe Brattle Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, citizenship status, national origin, ancestry, sex, gender identity and expression, age, height, weight, domestic partner status, Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome or HIV status (AIDS/HIV status), genetic information, sexual orientation, disability (where the applicant or employee is qualified to perform the essential functions of the job with or without reasonable accommodation), marital status, veteran status, political affiliation, drug or alcohol abuse or alcoholism, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law.We encourage all applicants to click here to review our full Equal Employer Opportunity Statement.THE EMPLOYERThe Brattle Group answers complex economic, finance, and regulatory questions for corporations, law firms, and governments around the world. We are distinguished by the clarity of our insights and the credibility of our experts, which include leading international academics and industry specialists. Brattle has 500 talented professionals across North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. For more information, please visit brattle.com​.​​​​​

jobs.title: Fermentation Control Engineer at Novonesis
jobs.description: Employer: Novonesis Expires: 10/20/2026 Interested in a career that matters? At Novonesis, we are pushing the boundaries of fermentation technology by developing next-generation control strategies that enable higher productivity, increased robustness, and improved sustainability. As a Fermentation Control intern, you will join our Fermentation and Recovery Development team in our Development and Optimization of Microbes organization that is responsible for the development, scale-up, and optimization of microbe products, processes, and technologies. Our teams are composed of scientists and researchers with diverse backgrounds that use a wide array of lab-, pilot-, and production-scale equipment, plus advanced data and digitalization tools, to develop and launch new products. We also collaborate with colleagues globally to take advantage of our combined knowledge in industrial microbiology. About the Role As a Fermentation Control Intern, you will work alongside Scientists and Research Associates to enhance fermentation performance, productivity, and process robustness, with a particular focus on Bacillus and yeast production processes. Specifically, you will implement and test a new fermentation control strategy on our bench and pilot fermentation systems while gaining experience with fermentation equipment and utilities, sensors, and programming strategies. What you’ll Need to Be Successful We are looking for students who are currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in: Chemical Engineering Biochemical Engineering Biological Engineering Mechanical Engineering Or a related technical discipline Required Qualifications and Competencies Minimum 3.0 GPA Strong analytical and problem-solving skills Interest in fermentation, process equipment, sensors, and programming controls Strong communication and collaboration skills Ability to work independently while contributing to team objectives Strong organizational skills and attention to detail Proficiency in basic mechanical equipment Sophomore standing or higher at the time of application Ability to arrange your own housing and transportation Any hands-on or classroom experience with advanced fermentation tools is a welcome bonus, but not required Ways of Working / Working Conditions Full-time internship assignment lasting approximately 10 weeks Located on-site in Morrisville, NC Exposure to Research and Development, analytical equipment, fermentation equipment and controls Use of required personal protective equipment (PPE) when in the laboratory Collaboration with cross-functional teams in the areas of microbial physiology, advanced process control, data science and AI CompensationExpected salary: $23/hr Relevant Information Program Dates: May 24th, 2027, to July 30th, 2027 Position Type: Temporary position payrolled through a third-party provider Application Deadline: October 15, 2026

Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow, and profoundly impact health for humanity. Learn more at jnj.comAs guided by Our Credo, Johnson & Johnson is responsible to our employees who work with us throughout the world. We provide an inclusive work environment where each person is considered as an individual. At Johnson & Johnson, we respect the diversity and dignity of our employees and recognize their merit.Job Function: Career ProgramsJob Sub Function: Non-LDP Intern/Co-OpJob Category:Career ProgramAll Job Posting Locations:San Diego, California, United States of AmericaJob Description:The Summer Graduate Intern, Translational Systems Toxicology, will join the multidisciplinary Translational Safety team within Preclinical Sciences and Translational Safety (PSTS) and gain hands-on experience supporting proteomics-based translational research. The intern will contribute to the development, optimization, and evaluation of sample preparation workflows for mass spectrometry-based proteomics, with a focus on improving robustness, throughput, scalability, and automation readiness across a variety of biological sample types, including blood- and tissue-derived samples. Key ResponsibilitiesSupporting the development, optimization, and evaluation of proteomics sample preparation workflows for biological samples, including blood- and tissue-derived matricesAssessing and comparing sample preparation approaches to improve analytical performance, reproducibility, throughput, and suitability for downstream mass spectrometry analysisExploring strategies to enable robust proteomic analysis from challenging or limited-volume samples, when appropriateDeveloping and adapting sample preparation workflows for laboratory automation platforms such as the Agilent AssayMAP BravoCollaborating with cross-functional scientists to design experiments, analyze results, and interpret findingsPerforming protein extraction, digestion, peptide cleanup, and other proteomics sample preparation procedures using established laboratory practicesAnalyzing experimental data and summarizing results using appropriate software and computational toolsMaintain clear experimental records, troubleshoot technical challenges, and communicate progress, results, and recommendations to cross-functional collaboratorsSummarize the project in a final presentation/poster and provide a concise, reproducible workflow and recommendations for future developmentRequired QualificationsAvailability to participate in a Summer 2027 internship program, with expected dates ranging from May-August 2027 or mid-June to mid-September 2027.Currently pursuing a Master's or PhD degree in Biochemistry, Analytical Chemistry, Proteomics, or a related scientific field and enrolled at an accredited university during the internship periodCandidates must have completed at least one year of graduate study by Summer 2027. Students entering their second or third year of a Master's or PhD program are encouraged to applyHands-on laboratory experience with biological samples and fundamental techniques such as accurate pipetting, buffer preparation, centrifugation, and sample handlingAbility to plan and execute experiments with appropriate guidance, maintain organized records, and work safely in a laboratory environmentStrong analytical, problem-solving, verbal communication, written communication, and collaboration skillsScientific curiosity, self-motivation, and the ability to work both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary teamPreferred QualificationsPrior experience with proteomics or mass spectrometry sample preparation, particularly low-input, blood-derived, or cell-based samplesFamiliarity with common proteomic sample-preparation methods, including in-solution digestion, S-Trap, SP3, or peptide cleanup workflows Experience with liquid-handling automation or the Agilent AssayMAP Bravo platformExposure to LC-MS/MS instrumentation, including Bruker timsTOF systems, and proteomics data-analysis software such as SpectronautWorking knowledge of R, Python, or another language used for scientific data analysisExperience handling blood, PBMCs, or samples from humans and preclinical species is beneficialCandidate Eligibility RequirementsCandidates must:Be authorized to work in the US without current or future sponsorship requirements.Remain actively enrolled in their academic program throughout the entire internship period.Be available to work 40 hours per week during the internship.Should have a minimum GPA of 3Permanently authorized to work in the U.S., must not require sponsorship of an employment visa (e.g., H-1B or green card) at the time of application or in the future. jobs.feedName: Andrew J. Anagnost College of Engineering and Computer Science
jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern - Tools and Prototypes at Quantum Signal AI
jobs.description: Employer: Quantum Signal AI Expires: 10/21/2026 This is a paid internship. Compensation for this position begins at $29.00 per hour.Role Summary: Quantum Signal AI (QSAI) is looking for a Software Engineering Intern – Tools and Prototypes to help develop engineering tooling and prototype software for the summer of 2027. Our applications range from specialized engineering tools to prototypes for advanced vehicle features that are used by engineers, researchers, and designers at Ford and QSAI. Interns will work alongside experienced engineers throughout the software development lifecycle and gain hands-on experience solving real engineering problems in a fast-paced R&D environment. A standout candidate will have experience in compiled languages (C++, Go, etc.), scripting languages (Python, JavaScript, etc.), web development, and software projects outside of an academic setting. We value the ability to quickly learn new technology to meet changing requirements, so a desire to learn is important! Location: Saline, Michigan (In-person). Our “historic schoolhouse” office supports hands-on collaboration, mentorship, and real-time problem solving. What You’ll Do (Essential Functions): Contribute to projects across the full Software Development Lifecycle, from design and implementation, to testing and release management Collaborate within varied project teams to develop tooling to improve engineering workflows Translate ideas, specifications, and/or requirements into high-quality implementations Tackle the challenges of learning, integrating, and leveraging a range of software tools and technologies as needed Develop documentation for software, processes, and projects Create and maintain build processes and CI/CD pipelines What You’ll Bring (Minimum Requirements): Current enrollment in an undergraduate degree-seeking program, pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related field Maintaining student status for the entire duration of the internship, including the academic term immediately following the internship Strong understanding of computer science fundamentals including data structures, algorithms, object-oriented programming, debugging, networking, and file systems Previous work/internship or academic club experience developing software Proficiency developing software in a compiled language (C++, Go, etc.) Experience with scripting languages (Python, JavaScript, etc.) Experience working in both Linux- and Windows-based environments Familiarity with web development (HTML, CSS, JS, etc.) Bonus Points For: Coursework or equivalent experience in operating systems, databases, compilers, concurrency, and other high level computer science topics Experience with REST APIs, either through integrating with existing APIs or designing APIs for downstream consumers Experience with modern web development frameworks and technologies (Node.js, React, Typescript, Flask, etc.) Experience with cloud-based development/deployment via GCP or equivalent cloud provider Experience integrating Identity and Access Management (IAM) solutions into an application (Microsoft Entra, RBAC, MSAL, authentication and authorization APIs) You may not check every box, or your experience may look a little different from what we've outlined, but if you are excited about this role and think you can bring value to Quantum Signal AI, we encourage you to apply! What You’ll Get: Frequent collaboration with a diverse set of teams at QSAI A rare level of work variety and hands-on experience A relaxed, fun community and environment in which to solve interesting problems Opportunity to participate in a 401(k) savings plan Ford AX-Plan vehicle discounts Mentorship-focused learning that emphasizes engineering fundamentals, hands-on problem solving, and understanding the underlying principles behind the systems we build. Other perks to fuel creativity such as an on-site gymnasium, free drinks and snacks, and a variety of optional team activities Candidates for positions with Quantum Signal AI must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Verification of employment eligibility will be required at the time of hire. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position. About QSAI: Founded in 1999, Quantum Signal grew up developing intelligent algorithms and AI. As our engineering R&D services expanded, we later sharpened our focus on applications and technology related to mobility, sensing, perception, autonomy, and simulation. In 2019 we became Quantum Signal AI, a subsidiary of Ford Motor developing technologies to advance their R&D efforts. We build solutions to enhance the capability, robustness, safety, and acceptance of intelligent ground vehicles in an effort to make transportation more effective and efficient for all. While AI is part of our name, our internship program emphasizes building fundamental engineering knowledge, analytical thinking, and practical problem-solving skills. We want interns to understand how and why systems work through hands-on experience, mentorship, and experimentation, rather than simply relying on tools to provide answers. Our HQ in the historic Union School in Saline, MI is the perfect playground to develop this cutting-edge technology and we’re always looking for smart folks who like new challenges, learning new skills, and technical variety.

jobs.description: Employer: Scalp Trade Expires: 10/21/2026 We are seeking a driven and intellectually curious C++ Software Developer Intern to join our dynamic trading firm. This is an exceptional opportunity to gain hands-on experience building high-performance trading systems while contributing meaningfully to our operations. You will work closely with experienced engineers in a mentorship-rich environment, learning cutting-edge low-latency systems design, trading infrastructure, and modern C++ development practices. This internship is designed to accelerate your growth as a software engineer while you help develop tools and strategies that directly impact our trading operations. If you thrive on learning, enjoy solving complex technical problems, and want to understand how financial technology works at scale, this is the role for you. Required Skills & QualificationsStrong Foundation in C++: Solid grasp of C++ fundamentals (STL, memory management, move semantics, templates). Production experience not required; demonstrated projects or coursework show readiness.Core CS Fundamentals: Comfortable with data structures, algorithms, and basic systems concepts (threading, process synchronization).Quick Learner: Able to rapidly pick up new tools, libraries, and frameworks with minimal guidance.Linux Familiarity: Comfortable working in Linux environments; shell scripting and command-line tools are a plus.Collaborative Mindset: Excellent communication skills; eager to learn from mentors and ask clarifying questions. Preferred Skills Multi-threading Experience: Practical familiarity with concurrent programming, thread safety, and synchronization primitives.Network Programming: Exposure to socket programming, TCP/IP, or distributed system basics.Additional Languages: Proficiency in Python, C#, or other systems languages broadens your perspective.Financial Markets Interest: Curiosity about trading, equities, options, or how financial markets work—we teach the rest.Database Exposure: Familiarity with SQL or understanding of how databases store and retrieve data at scale.Version Control & Tooling: Experience with Git, debugging tools (gdb, valgrind), or profilers (perf, flamegraph). Personal Attributes Intellectual Curiosity: Genuine interest in understanding how systems work, from code to infrastructure to business outcomes.Growth Mindset: Embrace challenges and feedback as opportunities to learn. We expect you to grow significantly over the internship.Ownership & Initiative: Proactive in seeking learning opportunities and taking on well-scoped responsibilities with minimal oversight.Adaptability: Comfortable with ambiguity and rapid changes; thriving in a fast-paced, high-performance environment.Collaborative Problem-Solving: Strong analytical skills with a preference for brainstorming and learning from teammates.Passion for Technology: Excitement about staying current with modern C++ and high-performance systems. What You'll GainHands-On Production Experience: Work in a real, production trading environment—not a sandbox. Your code runs strategies that generate revenue.Mentorship from Experts: Learn directly from senior engineers with deep expertise in low-latency systems, C++, and financial technology.Comprehensive Technical Knowledge: Understand high-performance systems design, from kernel tuning to network stack optimization.Career Acceleration: Build a portfolio of impactful projects and establish relationships with leaders in fintech.Potential for Conversion: Strong performers are considered for full-time roles upon graduation or at the conclusion of the internship. Compensation: This internship is paid at $7,000 per month for the program.

Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact. Engineering Intern Opportunities for Students Interns may support one or more engineering areas based on business need, candidate background, and location availability. Examples of work in each area are listed below. Research & Development Engineering Support design, development, analysis, and testing of engineering solutions during research and product development phases. Support safety testing, regulatory compliance, and transfer of products from development into manufacturing. Apply engineering fundamentals to real design, testing, and system-level challenges. Understand how safety, quality, and regulatory requirements influence engineering decisions. Operations Engineering Design and support manufacturing processes, procedures, and production layouts for assemblies, equipment, machining, and material handling. Provide technical and sustaining engineering support within manufacturing environments, including equipment and process improvements. Contribute to continuous improvement efforts focused on quality, efficiency, and production yield. Quality Engineering Develop, apply, and maintain quality standards and protocols for materials, components, and finished products. Collaborate with engineering, manufacturing, and supplier teams to support quality requirements and compliance. Support reliability studies, data analysis, and evaluation of design or test methods to achieve product reliability targets. Great for students who want to: Understand how quality systems and standards help ensure medical products are safe and compliant. Work cross-functionally to support quality and reliability across the product lifecycle. Build experience using data, testing, and process evaluation to support engineering decisions. spreadsheets, and trend summaries.Learn how customer requirements, company standards, and regulatory expectations are communicated and applied on projects.Training and Safety CommunicationHelp prepare materials and logistics for new-hire orientation, safety talks, contractor training, and other learning activities.Observe experienced trainers and safety professionals and assist during classes or meetings as assigned.Develop clear, audience-appropriate safety messages, toolbox-talk content, posters, or presentations for review.Practice communicating safety expectations respectfully with employees at different levels of the organization.Seek feedback and improve the clarity, accuracy, and usefulness of assigned safety communications.Incident Prevention and Continuous ImprovementObserve the incident-review process and learn how facts, contributing factors, root causes, and corrective actions are documented.Assist with preparation or organization of information for incident reports, safety reviews, and prevention follow-up.Review observation or training information to identify themes and suggest practical prevention ideas for consideration.Participate in lessons-learned discussions and complete an internship capstone that supports a practical safety improvement.Perform other related duties as assigned within the intern’s training, supervision, and authorization.What You Will LearnPieper Electric’s people-first safety culture and the responsibility to speak up.Hazard recognition, pre-task planning, jobsite observations, safe work practices, and incident prevention.How safety professionals partner with field leadership, project teams, employees, customers, and contractors.How safety programs, training, documentation, observations, and corrective actions support consistent execution.The role of applicable regulations, customer expectations, company standards, and continuous improvement in construction safety.Professional communication, confidentiality, accountability, and problem-solving in office and field environments.QualificationsCurrently pursuing an associate or bachelor’s degree in Occupational Safety and Health, Environmental Health and Safety, Construction Management, Engineering, Industrial Hygiene, Risk Management, or a related field.Interest in construction safety, electrical construction, field operations, training, or risk prevention.Basic proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams; willingness to learn company safety systems and technical tools.Ability to travel locally to project sites and work in both office and active construction environments as the assignment requires.Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation may be required based on project and jobsite assignments.Core Skills and BehaviorsPositive safety attitude and personal integrity. jobs.title: Virtual Design & Construction Intern at Pieper Electric, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Pieper Electric, Inc. - Pieper Electric, Inc Expires: 10/22/2026 Job DescriptionPosition Summary BIM is something we use. VDC is how we use digital information and technology to plan, coordinate, and improve how we build. As a Virtual Design & Construction Intern at Pieper Electric, you will learn how Building Information Modeling (BIM) supports the larger Virtual Design and Construction (VDC) process. You will gain hands-on experience using digital construction tools that support planning and field execution through model navigation, clash detection, constructability reviews, layout, and prefabrication. Working alongside BIM Specialists, Detailing Specialists, Project Managers, field leaders, and other project partners, you will help develop and coordinate constructible electrical models and drawings that connect design information to how work is planned, fabricated, laid out, and installed in the field. This internship is designed for students who enjoy technology, problem-solving, spatial thinking, and seeing how things are built. You do not need to know every BIM platform before joining us. We are looking for students who are curious, detail-oriented, willing to learn, and interested in understanding how digital models can be used to solve real construction challenges. Interns will receive guidance, feedback, and opportunities to take ownership of defined assignments under appropriate supervision. Values and Ways of Working At Pieper Electric, we believe in the Power to Serve and the Pursuit of Excellence. Our values, a Servant’s Heart, Wisdom, Integrity, Courage, Humility, and Passion, guide how we learn, collaborate, support the field, and serve our customers and teammates. As an intern, you will be encouraged to ask questions, share ideas, take initiative, and learn from experienced professionals while contributing to a safe and respectful team environment. Essential Responsibilities Safety and Field Engagement Complete required safety training and follow all company, customer, and jobsite requirements.Participate in supervised jobsite and prefabrication shop visits to understand how model information translates to installation.Learn how BIM supports safer planning, constructability, layout, prefabrication, and field execution.Promptly communicate safety concerns, field observations, or differences between modeled conditions and field conditions.BIM Modeling and Model Navigation Learn to navigate, review, create, and update 3D electrical models using Revit and other company BIM platforms.Assist with modeling electrical systems and components in support of coordination, constructability, prefabrication, layout, and installation.Review project drawings, specifications, submittals, and other available project information to support accurate model development.Update models as design information, coordination decisions, and field conditions change.Prepare model views and information that help project and field teams understand planned installation.Coordination, Clash Detection and Constructability Participate in BIM coordination and constructability reviews with project teams and trade partners.Learn how electrical systems are coordinated with architectural, structural, mechanical, plumbing, fire protection, and other building systems.Assist with identifying, documenting, and resolving clashes or spatial conflicts before installation.Review modeled routing and installation approaches with constructability, access, sequencing, and field execution in mind.Support approved model revisions resulting from coordination and constructability reviews.Detailing, Layout and Field Execution Assist with coordinated drawings, installation details, layouts, point drawings, and other field-ready information generated from or supported by BIM.Learn to interpret electrical symbols, one-lines, schedules, construction drawings, and model information.Support digital and model-based layout activities used to accurately locate electrical work in the field.Help prepare clear information for field teams and incorporate field feedback into models and drawings as directed.Prefabrication Support Learn how coordinated BIM content supports prefabrication and assembly planning.Assist with models, drawings, dimensions, material information, and documentation used to support prefabricated electrical assemblies.Participate in prefabrication shop visits to see how digital construction information becomes physical assemblies.Help maintain alignment between model information, prefabrication requirements, and planned field installation.Project Documentation and BIM Quality Maintain organized and accurate models, drawings, revisions, and project files.Perform assigned model and drawing quality checks for accuracy, completeness, and compliance with established standards.Support installation, record, and as-built documentation as directed.Follow company standards for file naming, version control, model organization, and documentation.Communication and Team Collaboration Collaborate with BIM, detailing, project management, prefabrication, field, and trade partners.Participate in team and coordination meetings and track assigned follow-up items.Ask questions when project requirements, design intent, or model information are unclear.Seek feedback, apply lessons learned, and communicate changes or potential delays to assigned work.Contribute ideas that improve BIM workflows, constructability, coordination, or the flow of information to the field.Learning and Continuous Improvement Participate in BIM software training, mentorship, and technical learning opportunities.Develop an understanding of how BIM fits within VDC and supports a project from preconstruction and coordination through prefabrication, installation, and closeout.Build familiarity with model navigation, clash detection, constructability reviews, layout, prefabrication, and other digital construction workflows.Explore career opportunities in BIM, detailing, VDC, and electrical construction.Complete a capstone or project assignment that provides a practical contribution to the team.

jobs.title: Hardware Test Engineering Co-Op at Delta Faucet Company
jobs.description: Employer: Delta Faucet Company - Delta Faucet HQ- Indianapolis, IN Expires: 10/23/2026 At Delta Faucet, we are committed to transforming everyday experiences with water through innovative products and exceptional service. As a leader in the plumbing industry, we take pride in our dedication to quality, sustainability, and customer satisfaction. We believe that diverse perspectives strengthen our mission to create solutions that inspire and elevate the lives of all our customers. We welcome individuals from all backgrounds to join us on this journey toward inclusivity and excellence. Your Role at Delta FaucetDelta Faucet Company has an opportunity for a Hardware Engineering Co-op to join our Connected Water Team to help deliver the next generation of product features and technology to our customers. In this role, you will support the development of new digital products through hands-on work with embedded systems and real product hardware. You will spend most of your days in the lab doing hands-on and varied tasks: soldering and reworking assemblies, programming and bringing up circuit boards, running electrical and functional tests, laying out PCBs, and keeping our engineering lab and its equipment running as smoothly as possible.You will report to the engineering manager and sit with the project teams, not apart from them. Within your first few weeks you will be assigned specific tasks, projects, and test processes to own — meaning you make the calls there, you document how it works, and you are the person others ask about it. When you find a better way to do something, we want to hear it, and we will give you a straight answer either way. Every part of the role is scoped so that the skills you leave with — test methodology, debugging discipline, documentation, lab ownership — are the ones that help you with the rest of your college work and prepare you for your future career. Responsibilities:Build and ReworkSolder, rework, and modify through-hole and surface-mount assemblies for prototypes, test fixtures, and engineering samples.Assemble and wire test fixtures, harnesses, and benchtop setups from schematics and written instructions.Program, flash, and bring up circuit boards; verify power rails, signal integrity, and basic functionality on new builds.Test and DebugExecute electrical, functional, and reliability tests on products and subassemblies, and record results accurately.Investigate test failures: reproduce the issue, isolate it to a component or subsystem, and document what you found so an engineer can act on it.Write and maintain basic test scripts and data-logging routines to automate repetitive measurements.Operate and troubleshoot standard bench equipment — oscilloscopes, DMMs, power supplies, function generators, data acquisition systems, environmental chambers.Design SupportProduce PCB layouts for test fixtures, adapter boards, and design revisions under engineering guidance.Review schematics and layouts for manufacturability and testability, and raise concerns before boards are ordered.Suggest product and process improvements based on what you observe on the benchLab and Calibration OwnershipOrganize and manage the engineering lab: equipment inventory, tool and fixture storage, consumable stock, workspace layout, and bench readiness.Run the equipment calibration program — track calibration due dates, coordinate with vendors, maintain certificates, and keep instruments in a known-good state.Establish and document standard operating procedures for test setups, lab safety, and equipment use so results are repeatable across people and across time.Maintain clear technical documentation: test reports, procedures, wiring diagrams, bring-up notes, and change records.Where this goesWe treat this co-op as the first step in a career here, not a temporary set of hands. The scope is designed to grow with you:In your first term, you will learn our products, our lab, and our test methods, supporting engineers on defined tasks.As you demonstrate judgment, you will take ownership of specific test areas, fixtures, and the calibration program — work that is yours, with your name on it.Strong co-ops are invited back for additional terms with expanded responsibility, and we actively look to convert high performers into full-time engineering or test roles at graduation.You will finish with a portfolio of real work: products you helped validate, fixtures you designed, procedures you wrote, and failures you tracked down. That is experience that transfers anywhere — and we would rather you build it here and stay. QualificationsCurrently pursuing a Bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology, or related fieldDemonstrated hands-on experience — coursework labs, senior design, competition teams (IEEE, Robotics, etc.), maker projects, or personal builds. Show us what you have made.Excellent soldering experience, including small components and SMT reworkFoundational understanding of analog and digital circuits. Comfort reading schematics and interpreting datasheets and basic specifications.Careful, methodical work habits. In test engineering, sloppy data is worse than no data, and this role is built on trustworthy measurements.Clear written communication — you will write procedures and failure reports that other people rely on.Familiarity with microcontrollers, embedded systems, and electronics lab equipmentStrong problem-solving skills, curiosity, and a willingness to learn in a hands-on engineering environmentInterest in IoT, connected products, or consumer electronics is a plus The target compensation for the role is $22.00 hour. Why Join Us?At Delta Faucet Company, our people are our greatest assets. We value different perspectives and fostering an inclusive environment. You’ll have the opportunity to shape the future of our brand, working alongside passionate professionals committed to excellence and innovation. Join us to lead progressive growth and make a significant impact within a leading organization.Here are some of the benefits we offer for your personal and professional growth:Culture: Recognized and award-winning reputation for equality, diversity and inclusion, flexibility, work-life balance, and more.Wellbeing: Comprehensive benefit plans; retirement, savings, tuition reimbursement, and employee incentive programs; resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.Learning & Development: LinkedIn Learning access; internal opportunities to work on projects cross-company.Social Impact: Four employee-led and self-directed Business Resource Groups; Paid volunteer day annually; Employees share their time, skills and talent with charities and nonprofit organizations across the U.S. and around the globe. Company: Delta Faucet Company Part time Delta Faucet Company (the “Company”) is an equal opportunity employer and we strive to employ the most qualified individuals for every position. The Company makes employment decisions only based on merit. It is the Company’s policy to prohibit discrimination in any employment opportunity (including but not limited to recruitment, employment, promotion, salary increases, benefits, termination and all other terms and conditions of employment) based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, pregnancy, religious creed, national origin, ancestry, age, physical/mental disability, medical condition, marital/domestic partner status, military and veteran status, height, weight or any other such characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. The Company is committed to complying with all applicable laws providing equal employment opportunities. This commitment applies to all people involved in the operations of the Company regardless of where the employee is located and prohibits unlawful discrimination by any employee of the Company. With more than 40 offices around the world, we offer insights and expertise to investors, companies, and governments.What you can expectJefferies Summer Interns have the unique opportunity to gain insight into a global, client-focused investment bank and experience an entrepreneurial environment where employees have the opportunity to make an immediate impact and are rewarded for performance. The work is fast paced, challenging, and intellectually stimulating. The ability to work under pressure and tight deadlines, be adaptable, and work both independently and as part of a team are essential traits of a successful candidate. Candidates should have a strong academic background and be pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree or equivalent program.Desired Background and SkillsCandidates pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Security, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related technical fieldExpected graduation between December 2027 and June 2028Programming or scripting experience in one or more of Python, Java, C#, JavaScript, SQL, Bash, PowerShell or VBAInterest in platform reliability, site reliability engineering, information security, cloud, infrastructure, enterprise applications or automationExposure to Linux, Unix or Windows; databases; networking; virtualization; containers; Kubernetes; or cloud platforms such as AWS and AzureFamiliarity with observability and DevOps practices, including Git, CI/CD, Prometheus, Grafana or related toolsExperience with APIs, data analysis, BI/reporting, workflow automation, Power Platform, UiPath or AI/ML is a plusStrong analytical, problem-solving, written and verbal communication skillsAbility to learn quickly, collaborate in a fast-paced global team and focus on reliability, security, operational excellence and disciplined deliveryWORK WITH US - Opportunities in Information TechnologyThe Jefferies Technology team is increasingly a source of revenue and competitive advantage for one of the fastest growing investment banking firms in the world. We deploy and manage the technology that keeps Jefferies running and our colleagues connected. jobs.description: Employer: Ameritas Life Insurance Corp Expires: 10/23/2026 Ameritas is seeking a User Experience (UX) Intern to enhance our customers’ digital experiences by researching user experience across our digital platforms. Position Location: This is a hybrid role (Cincinnati, OH or Lincoln, NE) working partially in-office and partially from home. Position Start Date: This internship will begin in May 2027. This will be a summer internship running May - August.What You’ll Do: Design intuitive, user-friendly digital experiences that align with project goals and customer needs. Translate complex challenges into clear, user-centered solutions. Conduct and analyze UX research to uncover insights and inform design decisions. Create prototypes and design deliverables that effectively communicate ideas to stakeholders. Collaborate with product owners, developers, and designers to ensure a seamless process from concept to launch. Partner with UI developers to align design intent with implementation. Support ongoing product iteration based on research, user feedback, and performance data. Contribute to design system consistency, accessibility standards, and current UX best practices. Participate in project meetings and advocate for the user perspective in cross-functional discussions. Explore ways to integrate AI tools into the design process (e.g., generating design variations, analyzing feedback, enhancing accessibility). Stay curious about emerging technologies, including AI, and how they can elevate the design process and user experience. What You Bring: Must be enrolled in a Master’s degree program at least half-time as defined by your institution studying Human-Computer Interaction, Design, or a related field for the entire duration of the internship. Able to commit to a full-time, 3-month summer internship. Full-time hours: 40 hours per week Prior experience in UX or digital product design (academic, internship, or personal projects). Familiarity with design tools such as Figma and Adobe Creative Suite. Basic understanding of front-end development (HTML, CSS); exposure to AI-assisted design techniques is a plus. Strong attention to detail and ability to translate requirements into interactive solutions. Clear communicator who collaborates well across teams. Awareness of accessibility guidelines, design systems, and web standards. Interest in applying AI tools and data-driven insights to improve design outcomes. Experience with generative AI tools and workflows is a strong advantage. Possess a growth mindset: comfortable with ambiguity, open to feedback, and eager to learn. Ability to manage multiple responsibilities within Agile/Scrum teams. Online portfolio or sample projects showcasing creative thinking and problem-solving skills required. Please submit link with resume. What we offer: At Ameritas, our mission is Fulfilling Life. We do that in many ways, but especially by helping people invest in themselves by offering trusted financial products and advice. Because we believe everyone should be happy, healthy, and financially secure, we work hard to provide trusted financial products and valued guidance, including individual life and disability insurance, employee benefits, retirement planning, investments, and wealth management services. Our company motto is “Fulfilling Life” and we take that job seriously, with a heavy commitment to volunteering and community support, employee well-being, and providing quality products and services that help our customers create a brighter future. Being a mutual-based organization, the return on our investment goes back into the company, to benefit our members/customers. We’re committed to professional development, opportunity, inclusion, and diversity. Team building and collaboration are also priorities. An Equal Opportunity Employer Ameritas has a reputation as a company that cares, and because everyone should feel safe bringing their authentic, whole self to work, we’re committed to an inclusive culture and diverse workplace, enriched by our individual differences. We are an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer that hires based on qualifications, positive attitude, and exemplary work ethic, regardless of sex, race, color, national origin, religion, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or any other characteristic protected by law. Application DeadlineThis position will be open for a minimum of 3 business days or until filled.This position is not open to individuals who are temporarily authorized to work in the U.S.

jobs.description: Employer: Dancephreakz Expires: 10/23/2026 Phrkz Network | DancePhreakzLocation: Los Angeles County, CA | HybridPosition Type: Part-Time InternshipSchedule: Approximately 8–15 hours per weekCompensation: Paid InternshipAbout the Organization:DancePhreakz is a dynamic, women-owned, and BIPOC-led dance and entertainment production company that is revolutionizing the industry. We bring creativity, energy, and authenticity to the world of dance and movement. Through our four divisions—Production, Apparel, Academy, and our newly acquired studio and event space—we aim to build a platform where BIPOC movement artists thrive, fostering a community that is unapologetically fierce, creative, and ready to make an impact.About Phrkz NetworkPhrkz Network is a new media and entertainment division of DancePhreakz launching in 2026. The Network is an evolution of DancePhreakz's production work into a dedicated home for original shows, podcasts, interviews, digital series, visual projects, documentaries, and culture-driven entertainment.As we build the Network, we're looking for emerging editors who want hands-on experience helping shape the look, pace, and storytelling style of an original digital entertainment platform.About the InternshipWe're seeking two Video Editor & Post-Production Interns to join our growing production team.This is an editing-first position for creatives who already have hands-on editing experience and want to strengthen their portfolio while working on real entertainment programming.You'll edit both long-form and short-form content, including full-length video podcasts, original shows, multi-camera productions, interviews, trailers, teasers, YouTube content, Reels, TikToks, and YouTube Shorts.We want editors who understand that great editing isn't simply cutting footage together. It's about finding the story, creating a hook, controlling pacing, capturing personality, and making viewers want to keep watching.Our creative inspiration comes from modern digital entertainment and culture-driven media platforms such as Hoorae Media, Keytv, Complex, The Black Effect, SpringHill, REVOLT, Joe Budden Podcast, and similar creator-led networks. We're looking for editors interested in understanding what makes their content feel current, entertaining, polished, and highly shareable.What You'll DoLong-Form & Podcast EditingEdit full-length video podcasts, interviews, original shows, and digital series for YouTube and other platforms. Edit multi-camera productions and seamlessly switch between angles based on conversation, reactions, and story. Sync and edit multiple camera and audio sources. Edit and prepare audio versions of podcast episodes for Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and other podcast platforms. Perform color correction, dialogue cleanup, audio balancing, and basic sound design. Add intros/outros, lower thirds, graphics, captions, music, B-roll, and branded elements. Create engaging openings and maintain strong pacing throughout longer episodes. Short-Form & Promotional EditingTurn long-form episodes into compelling Reels, TikToks, and YouTube Shorts. Identify moments with strong hooks, reactions, humor, controversy, insight, or emotional impact. Create trailers, teasers, cold opens, episode promos, and highlight packages. Reframe and optimize content for vertical and horizontal formats. Understand that a 60-second social edit requires different pacing and storytelling than a 45-minute YouTube episode. Post-Production WorkflowOrganize raw footage, project files, audio, graphics, and final exports. Maintain organized editing projects that another editor can easily open and understand. Complete revisions based on producer/director notes. Export content according to platform specifications. Help maintain consistent editing and visual standards across Phrkz Network programming. Manage multiple assignments while meeting production deadlines.QualificationsMust reside in Los Angeles County, California.Currently enrolled in or recently graduated from a college/university program in film, media, communications, or a related field—or equivalent experience/portfolio.Previous video editing experience is required—this is not a learn-from-zero editing internship.Portfolio, demo reel, or work samples required.Proficiency in Adobe Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut Pro, AVID, or comparable professional editing software.Experience editing both short-form and/or long-form content.Strong understanding of storytelling, pacing, music, sound, reactions, and visual rhythm.Comfortable working with multi-camera footage.Basic knowledge of audio editing, color correction, captions, graphics, and exporting.Able to work independently and make creative decisions without requiring detailed instructions for every cut.Strong time management and ability to work within quick turnaround deadlines.Comfortable receiving notes, making revisions, and collaborating with producers and other editors.Interest in entertainment, pop culture, podcasts, music, dance, digital media, and original programming.Internship DetailsSchedule: 8–15 hours per week with flexible scheduling to accommodate classes or other commitments.Location: Hybrid—remote editing plus occasional on-site filming in Gardena, CA.Compensation: Paid internshipAcademic credit available if approved by your institution.Other Information:Exempt/Non-Exempt: ExemptEOE Statement: We are an equal employment opportunity employer.
